Legacy campaign

The Power You Don't Build (1962–1981)

The oil shocks of the 1970s are coming. If your customers can use less electricity, your California utility can buy less fuel.

Open the Legacy campaign↗ Your decisions ↓

Play the chapters in order. You carry the same utility from one generation to the next.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
1962
Generation
20 years

Your starting point

In 1962 you inherit the plants your earlier generations chose. If much of the fleet runs on oil, the price shocks of 1973 and 1979 will hit your fuel bill harder.

By the end of 1981, your efficiency programs need to save 5% of home and business electricity use.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Compare efficiency with new supply

    Estimate how much electricity a program would save before committing to another plant. Those savings can also reduce the fuel you buy today.

  2. 02

    Check the oil bill

    Look at how often your oil plants run and what else could supply those hours if fuel gets expensive.

  3. 03

    Measure the savings

    Check how much the programs actually cut household and business use. That tells you how far you are from the 5% goal.

How much fuel could you save by helping customers use less electricity?
